{{short description|Triangle with vertices at midpoints of another triangle's sides}}
[[File:Medial Triangle.svg|thumb|right|The red triangle is the medial triangle of the black. The endpoints of the red triangle coincide with the midpoints of the black triangle.]]

In [[Euclidean geometry]], the '''medial triangle''' or '''midpoint triangle''' of a [[triangle]] {{math|△''ABC''}} is the triangle with [[vertex (geometry)|vertices]] at the [[midpoint]]s of the triangle's sides {{mvar|AB}}, {{mvar|AC}}, and {{mvar|BC}}. It is the {{math|1=''n'' = 3}} case of the [[midpoint polygon]] of a [[polygon]] with {{mvar|n}} sides.  The medial triangle is not the same thing as the [[median triangle]], which is the triangle whose sides have the same lengths as the [[Median (geometry)|medians]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}.

Each side of the medial triangle is called a ''midsegment'' (or ''midline''). In general, a midsegment of a triangle is a line segment which joins the midpoints of two sides of the triangle. It is parallel to the third side and has a length  equal to half the length of the third side.

==Properties==
[[File:Mittendreieck.svg|thumb|upright=1.6|
{{mvar|M}}: [[circumcenter]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}, [[orthocenter]] of {{math|△''DEF''}}<br/>
{{mvar|N}}: [[incenter]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}, [[Nagel point]] of {{math|△''DEF''}}<br/>
{{mvar|S}}: [[centroid]] of {{math|△''ABC''}} and {{math|△''DEF''}}
]]

The medial triangle can also be viewed as the image of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} transformed by a [[Homothetic transformation|homothety]] centered at the [[centroid]] with ratio -1/2. Thus, the sides of the medial triangle are half and parallel to the corresponding sides of {{math|△''ABC''}}. Hence, the medial triangle is inversely [[Similarity (geometry)|similar]] and shares the same centroid and [[median (geometry)|medians]] with {{math|△''ABC''}}. It also follows from this that the [[perimeter]] of the medial triangle equals the [[semiperimeter]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}, and that the [[area]] is one quarter of the area of {{math|△''ABC''}}. Furthermore, the four triangles that the original triangle is subdivided into by the medial triangle are all mutually [[congruence (geometry)|congruent]] by [[Triangle#Similarity and congruence|SSS]], so their areas are equal and thus the area of each is 1/4 the area of the original triangle.<ref name=PL>Posamentier, Alfred S., and Lehmann, Ingmar. ''[[The Secrets of Triangles]]'', Prometheus Books, 2012.</ref>{{rp|p.177}}

The [[orthocenter]] of the medial triangle coincides with the [[circumcenter]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}. This fact provides a tool for proving [[Euler line|collinearity of the circumcenter, centroid and orthocenter]]. The medial triangle is the [[pedal triangle]] of the circumcenter. The [[nine-point circle]] circumscribes the medial triangle, and so the nine-point center is the circumcenter of the medial triangle.

The [[Nagel point]] of the medial triangle is the [[incenter]] of its reference triangle.<ref name=ac>Altshiller-Court, Nathan. ''College Geometry''. Dover Publications, 2007.</ref>{{rp|p.161, Thm.337}} In particular, this means that the incenter of a triangle must lie in its medial triangle.<ref name=Franzsen>{{cite journal |url=http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2011volume11/FG201126.pdf |last=Franzsen |first=William N. |title=The distance from the incenter to the Euler line |journal=Forum Geometricorum |volume=11 |year=2011 |pages=231–236}}</ref>{{rp|p.233, Lemma 1}}

The incenter of the medial triangle is the [[Spieker center]] of its reference triangle.

A reference triangle's medial triangle is [[congruence (geometry)|congruent]] to the triangle whose vertices are the midpoints between the reference triangle's [[orthocenter]] and its vertices.<ref name=ac/>{{rp|p.103,#206;p.108,#1}}

A point in the interior of a triangle is the center of an [[Circumconic and inconic|inellipse]] of the triangle if and only if the point lies in the interior of the medial triangle.<ref name=Chakerian>Chakerian, G. D. "A Distorted View of Geometry." Ch. 7 in ''Mathematical Plums'' (R. Honsberger, editor). Washington, DC: Mathematical Association of America, 1979.</ref>{{rp|p.139}}

The medial triangle is the only [[inscribed figure|inscribed triangle]] for which none of the other three interior triangles has smaller area.<ref name=Torrejon>{{cite journal |last=Torrejon |first=Ricardo M. |title=On an Erdos inscribed triangle inequality |journal=Forum Geometricorum |volume=5 |year=2005 |pages=137–141 |url=http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2005volume5/FG200519index.html}}</ref>{{rp|p. 137}}

The reference triangle and its medial triangle are [[orthologic triangles]].

==Coordinates==
Let {{math|1=''a'' = {{abs|''BC''}}}}, {{math|1=''b'' = {{abs|''CA''}}}}, {{math|1=''c'' = {{abs|''AB''}}}} be the sidelengths of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.  [[Trilinear coordinates]] for the vertices of the medial triangle {{math|△''EFD''}} are given by:
<math display=block>\begin{array}{ccc}
  E =& 0           &:& \frac{1}{b} &:& \frac{1}{c} \\[2pt]
  F =& \frac{1}{a} &:& 0           &:& \frac{1}{c} \\[2pt]
  D =& \frac{1}{a} &:& \frac{1}{b} &:& \, 0
\end{array}</math>

==Anticomplementary triangle==
If {{math|△''EFD''}} is the medial triangle of {{math|△''ABC''}}, then {{math|△''ABC''}} is the '''anticomplementary triangle''' or '''antimedial triangle''' of {{math|△''EFD''}}. The anticomplementary triangle of {{math|△''ABC''}} is formed by three lines parallel to the sides of {{math|△''ABC''}}: the parallel to {{mvar|AB}} through {{mvar|C}}, the parallel to {{mvar|AC}} through {{mvar|B}}, and the parallel to {{mvar|BC}} through {{mvar|A}}.

[[Trilinear coordinates]] for the vertices of the triangle <math>\triangle E'F'D'</math> anticomplementary to <math>\triangle ABC</math> are given by:
<math display=block>\begin{array}{crrr}
  E' =& -\frac{1}{a} &:& \frac{1}{b} &:& \frac{1}{c} \\[2pt]
  F' =& \frac{1}{a} &:& -\frac{1}{b} &:& \frac{1}{c} \\[2pt]
  D' =& \frac{1}{a} &:& \frac{1}{b} &:& -\frac{1}{c}
\end{array}</math>

The name "anticomplementary triangle" corresponds to the fact that its vertices are the anticomplements of the vertices {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, and {{mvar|C}} of the reference triangle.  The vertices of the medial triangle are the complements of {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, and {{mvar|C}}.
